To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

PtdIns4 kinase is closely associated with actin cytoskeletal dynamics in guard cells of Commelina communis, and that PtdIns 4P and PtdIn 3P are involved in ABA-mediated actin cytoskelton dynamics in these cells.
PtdIns 4-and 3-kinasemodulate actin filament rearrangement in guard cells of Commelina communis in response to ABB, at least in pa, via generation of ROS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of actin filaments in plant cells, and we have demonstrated that PtdIns 4-phosphate and PtdIns 5-phosphate are involved in this regulation.
the role of PtdIns 4-phosphate and PtdIns 5-phosphate in the regulation of actin dynamics.
the role of phosphoinositides in actin dynamics in day flower guard cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PtdIns 4-phosphatidylinositols (PtdInsPs) regulate actin dynamics via ROS production in guard cells.
PtdIns 4 and 3-kinasses, which generate PtdIns3 and PtdIns3,4P2, are important regulators of actins in plants.
PtdIns4,5P3, PtdIns3,4, and 5P3, and PtdIns3 and 4P regulate actins in plants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PtdIns 4-phosphatase (PIP4P) is a key enzyme that regulates actin dynamics via PtdIns3p and ROS in plant guard cells.
PtdIns(4)P and Ptd(3,4)P(2) play important roles in actin re-organization in plant cells.
ABA-induced actomyosin contractility in guard cells is modulated by the balance between PtdIns3- and PtdIn4-kinases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PtdIns(4,5)bisP and PtdIn(3,5)bis-P are the key lipid regulators for the actin cytokeleton in plants.
